title: Advanced AI can move the fiscal bottleneck from taxing labor and consumption toward taxing autonomous productive systems
source_unit: NBER Working Paper 34873 theoretical primer on public finance under AI transformation
geography: General public-finance framework with implications for advanced economies and U.S.-relevant labor, consumption, and AI tax bases

denominator.unit: theoretical public-finance model and policy framework

current_tax_base_risk.value: if AI displaces human labor, labor-income and human-consumption tax bases can erode

stage_one_tax_response.value: in an early displacement stage, consumption taxation can become a primary revenue instrument and differential commodity taxation can become more relevant

stage_two_tax_base.value: when autonomous AI systems produce most economic value and absorb a growing share of resources, taxing human consumption may become inadequate

autonomous_system_tax.value: taxing autonomous AI production is framed as an optimal-harvesting problem, with the tax rate depending on the human rate of time preference

observations.method: Theoretical public-finance analysis of optimal taxation in two stages of AI transformation, distinguishing labor displacement from autonomous systems producing most economic value.
observations.uncertainty: This is a conceptual and model-based primer, not an observed adoption estimate, revenue forecast, welfare estimate, or implemented policy analysis. Results depend on assumptions about AI capability, displacement, production, ownership, consumption, and political feasibility.
observations.subgroup: Workers, consumers, firms owning or deploying AI systems, taxpayers, beneficiaries of public spending, and governments choosing tax and redistribution instruments.
observations.counterinterpretation: AI may complement labor, create new tasks, expand the tax base, or be taxed through existing firm and capital systems; ownership, bargaining, transfers, and international coordination can alter the modeled incidence.

related_sources.claim: NBER DOI record for the working paper.
Official working-paper PDF for the theoretical tax framework.

boundary: This record adds a theoretical AI-to-tax-base and state-capacity mechanism. It does not establish realized AI displacement, a U.S. revenue loss, a feasible autonomous-system tax, ownership concentration, household incidence, or international tax coordination.
